what: Finding 1: plan updates the Markdown sub-procedure but omits the shell-owned Step 10/12 run_rebase_rebump path
scenario_or_breakage: scripts/ship-pr.sh currently owns Step 10/12 rebase plus re-bump, still calls drop-bump-commit.sh without --allow-changelog-only, and has no proposed commit-changelog step after apply-bump.sh, so the CI/merge path can retain the old stall shape or drift from the documented CHANGELOG commit shape
suggested_fix: Add scripts/ship-pr.sh to UPDATED files; pass --allow-changelog-only in run_rebase_rebump, add the same separate CHANGELOG commit behavior or explicitly document why shell Step 10/12 does not update CHANGELOG, and cover it in test-ship-pr.sh

what: Finding 2: new commit-changelog.sh is specified as a direct git commit -m wrapper instead of reusing the repo commit primitive
scenario_or_breakage: Direct git commit bypasses git-commit.sh trailer and scoping policy; if validation later drifts, unrelated staged files can be captured and CHANGELOG commits become inconsistent with other /implement commit points
suggested_fix: Implement commit-changelog.sh as validation plus scripts/git-commit.sh -m "Update CHANGELOG for $version" --only CHANGELOG.md, or document and test an intentional --no-trailer exception

what: Finding 3: plan changes implement-finalize.sh to call commit-changelog.sh but omits the existing Step 8a harness stub update
scenario_or_breakage: The harness copies implement-finalize.sh into a sandbox and only creates git-amend-add.sh; after the proposed call-site change, make test-step-8a-changelog fails because commit-changelog.sh is missing
suggested_fix: Add a commit-changelog.sh stub or copy the real helper and required dependencies in build_sandbox, then assert CHANGELOG_STATUS=updated still works with the separate commit shape

what: Finding 4: proposed new Test 16-19 names collide with existing Test 16-20 numbering
scenario_or_breakage: The plan says add tests after existing Test 15, but this file already has numbered tests 16 through 20, making the harness harder to maintain and review
